statement: In JavaScript, evaluating `typeof NaN` returns the string `"number"`.
explanation: `NaN` is the numeric result of an invalid operation, so its primitive type stays `number`. The practical trap: it is unequal to itself, so `x === NaN` is always false — detect it with `Number.isNaN`.
subject: design-patterns
codeHtml:
const result = 0 / 0; // NaN
console.log(typeof result); // "number"
